data.description:
# Live Jira probe command to pre-populate mapping config

## Context / Problem

The mapping config (S1–S5) is hand-editable in `rebar.toml`, but forcing a human to
transcribe every Jira issue type, status, link type, hierarchy level, and priority by hand
is error-prone and hostile to setup. The live PoC (this session) proved every axis is
interrogable read-only via Jira REST v3. A probe command should observe a live Jira project
and emit a suggested `[tool.rebar.mapping]` block so setup is ergonomic and transcription-
error-free. Transitions are only partially discoverable (the API returns transitions from
the *current* status only, not the full workflow graph), so the probe must flag them
best-effort rather than claim completeness.

## Approach

Add a **read-only** probe under the bridge command surface: `rebar bridge probe <PROJECT>`.
It calls the proven endpoints — `/project/{key}/statuses` (issue types + per-type
statuses), `/issuetype` (`hierarchyLevel`), `/issueLinkType`, `/priority`, and
`/issue/createmeta/{key}/issuetypes/{id}` (required create fields) — and emits a suggested
mapping block: the discovered vocabulary lists (`statuses`, `issue_types`, `link_types`,
`hierarchy`), identity-mapped `status_map`/`type_map`/`link_map`/`priority_map` seeds, and
`create_defaults` stubs for required-beyond-baseline create fields. Default behavior
**emits TOML to stdout** (never writes); `--write` merges it into the resolved config file
under `projects.<KEY>` (never clobbering existing hand edits — deep-merge, existing keys
win). Transitions are recorded as a best-effort comment/flag in the emitted block, not as a
completeness claim. The probe reuses the existing Jira transport (S1 capability descriptor
supplies which axes to probe); it stays strictly read-only against Jira.

## Scope

- A new probe module under `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/`
  (Jira-specific interrogation) + a neutral emit/merge helper.
- `rebar bridge probe` CLI wiring in the bridge command surface.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_probe.py` (new) — against a faked REST client.

## Testing

- **Emit shape (unit, faked REST):** given canned `/statuses`, `/issuetype`,
  `/issueLinkType`, `/priority` responses, the emitted TOML contains the discovered
  vocabulary lists and identity-seed maps under `projects.<KEY>` — asserted on the parsed
  emitted TOML.
- **Read-only:** the probe issues only GET requests — asserted on the faked client's
  recorded method set (no POST/PUT/DELETE).
- **`--write` deep-merges (failure-safe):** an existing hand-edited `status_map` entry
  survives `--write` (existing key wins); a new discovered key is added — asserted on the
  post-merge config.
- **Transitions flagged best-effort:** the emitted block marks transitions best-effort and
  does not present a full transition graph — asserted on the emitted text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar bridge probe <PROJECT>` emits a suggested `[tool.rebar.mapping]` block with
  discovered vocabulary + identity-seed maps to stdout by default — verified by
  `test_probe.py::test_probe_emits_mapping`.
- [ ] The probe is read-only (GET-only against Jira) — verified by
  `test_probe.py::test_probe_is_read_only`.
- [ ] `--write` deep-merges into `projects.<KEY>` without clobbering existing entries —
  verified by `test_probe.py::test_probe_write_preserves_edits`.
- [ ] Transitions are emitted as best-effort, not as a completeness claim — verified by
  `test_probe.py::test_probe_transitions_best_effort`.

Test tier: **in-process unit with a faked REST client** — the oracle is the emitted TOML,
the recorded HTTP method set, and the post-merge config; a live tier is unnecessary because
the interrogation-to-TOML logic is what's under test and the REST boundary is injected. (A
manual live smoke against REB is the setup validation, not an automated gate — REB has no
guaranteed CI credential, so a live-only test would violate portability.)
data.title: Live Jira probe command to pre-populate mapping config
